hypotheses.text: Across all published TUBA4A-associated spastic ataxia kindreds (Torella et al. and Benkirane et al.), oculomotor signs (nystagmus and broken smooth pursuit) show near-complete penetrance (>85% of clinically evaluated cases), whereas cerebellar dysarthria is present in fewer than 50% of affected patients.
hypotheses.rationale: In the index p.Glu415Lys kindreds (Torella et al.), nystagmus is documented in all 12 evaluated affected individuals (12/12) and broken smooth pursuit is nearly universal, while dysarthria is explicitly qualified as only occurring 'sometimes'. Testing whether this discrepancy holds when pooling with the multicentric cohort of Benkirane et al. (12 additional patients across diverse missense alleles) establishes whether oculomotor signs are primary diagnostic red flags compared to bulbar/speech involvement.

evidence.text: Torella et al. reported two families with 12 affected individuals carrying TUBA4A p.Glu415Lys presenting with spastic ataxia, displaying ocular movement abnormalities (nystagmus in 12/12, broken smooth pursuit), and dysarthria in only a subset of patients.

hypotheses.text: The emergence of cerebellar dysarthria in TUBA4A spastic ataxia (SPAX11) correlates strictly with advanced disease duration (>10 years from motor onset) rather than being an early presenting phenotype.
hypotheses.rationale: If oculomotor signs like gaze-evoked nystagmus and broken pursuit occur at symptom onset but speech remains normal until late in the disease, clinicians can exclude early-onset spastic ataxias characterized by early, severe bulbar involvement (such as ARSACS or certain SCA subtypes) when evaluating early spastic-ataxic patients.

evidence.text: In the initial characterization of TUBA4A p.Glu415Lys families, gait ataxia and pyramidal spasticity are the presenting features alongside nystagmus, whereas dysarthria is only inconsistently present ('sometimes dysarthria') among adult family members with varying disease durations.

hypotheses.text: De novo TUBA4A missense variants reported in Benkirane et al. produce a significantly higher incidence of early-onset dysarthria than the familial inherited p.Glu415Lys variant reported by Torella et al.
hypotheses.rationale: De novo mutations in tubulin genes typically exert stronger dominant-negative effects on microtubule lattice integration than mildly deleterious inherited variants. Comparing patient-level data between de novo cases and multi-generational familial cases will reveal whether speech motor pathways are preferentially vulnerable in de novo tubulinopathies.

new_directions.question_text: What is the exact individual-level breakdown of dysarthria severity, nystagmus type (horizontal, vertical, gaze-evoked, downbeat), and broken smooth pursuit in the supplementary tables of Benkirane et al. (2024)?
new_directions.rationale: Extracting the raw supplementary clinical tables from Benkirane et al. will allow exact pooled numerator/denominator calculations (e.g., n/24 total published SPAX11 patients) for speech and specific oculomotor sub-phenotypes.

new_directions.question_text: Do patients with TUBA4A-associated spastic ataxia demonstrate vestibulo-ocular reflex (VOR) abnormalities or saccadic dysmetria, and how do their oculomotor profiles compare directly to FGF14 (SCA27B) and AFG3L2 (SPAX5/SCA28)?
new_directions.rationale: Both SCA27B and SCA28 present with spasticity and downbeat/gaze-evoked nystagmus. Determining whether TUBA4A exhibits distinct saccadic abnormalities or downbeat nystagmus provides essential clinical bedside discriminator metrics.
